newsitem.title: USA: Ohio gov. says funding ruling calls for tax hike.
newsitem.headline: Ohio gov. says funding ruling calls for tax hike.

text.p: Ohio Gov. George Voinovich lashed out Tuesday against an Ohio Supreme Court ruling that found the state's system of funding education to be unconstitutional saying the decision was essentially calling for a massive tax hike.
Speaking at a news conference in Columbus, the Republican governor said Monday's 4 to 3 high court ruling was aimed at a multi-billion state tax increase to fund schools.
He added the ruling offered "minimal guidance" to lawmakers and would erode "the long-standing tradition of local decision making."

On Monday, a majority of justices ruled that the state's school funding system violates the Ohio Constitution, which the court said mandates a thorough and efficient system of common schools throughout the state.

Justices gave Ohio one year to overhaul the funding system, but made it clear they do not advocate a so-called "Robin Hood" approach that would siphon funds from richer districts for use in poorer districts. The ruling also rejected spending ceilings on affluent school districts.

Voinovich did not offer any plans for changing the state's current funding system, but emphasized the importance of passing a fiscal 1998-99 biennial budget that continues to address funding disparities among districts. He added that schools need to know what to expect in terms of funding from the state over the next bienium, which begins July 1.
Rating agency officials have said the ruling would not have any immediate affect on ratings for the state or school districts.
The ruling concluded a six-year court battle between a coalition of school districts and the state over school funding.
